stories.headline: Nvidia launches open-source Agent Toolkit at GTC with 17 enterprise software giants adopting

key_facts.fact: At GTC 2026 on March 16, Nvidia unveiled the Agent Toolkit, an open-source platform for building autonomous AI agents, with 17 enterprise software companies adopting it: Adobe, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Siemens, CrowdStrike, Atlassian, Cadence, Synopsys, IQVIA, Palantir, Box, Cohesity, Dassault Systèmes, Red Hat, Cisco, and Amdocs.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nvidia CEO unveiled the Agent Toolkit, an open-source platform for building autonomous AI agents, and then rattled off the names of the companies that will use it: Adobe, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Siemens, CrowdStrike, Atlassian, Cadence, Synopsys, IQVIA, Palantir, Box, Cohesity, Dassault Systèmes, Red Hat, Cisco and Amdocs.

key_facts.fact: The toolkit bundles four components: Nemotron open models, the AI-Q Blueprint for agentic search, cuOpt skills, and the new OpenShell open-source runtime that enforces policy-based security, network, and privacy guardrails for autonomous agents.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA Agent Toolkit provides open source models and software for enterprises and developers building tools that scale productivity by autonomously determining how to complete assigned tasks. It now includes NVIDIA OpenShell — an open source runtime that enforces policy-based security, network and privacy guardrails.

key_facts.fact: The AI-Q Blueprint, built with LangChain, achieved #1 on both DeepResearch Bench I (55.95) and DeepResearch Bench II (54.50), using a hybrid architecture with frontier and open models that cuts query costs by more than 50%.
key_facts.excerpt: Built with LangChain, the open source NVIDIA AI-Q Blueprint for agentic search tops DeepResearch Bench accuracy leaderboards — using a hybrid approach with both frontier and open models that can cut query costs in half.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang declared: 'Claude Code and OpenClaw have sparked the agent inflection point — extending AI beyond generation and reasoning into action. Employees will be supercharged by teams of frontier, specialized and custom-built agents.'
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Code and OpenClaw have sparked the agent inflection point — extending AI beyond generation and reasoning into action.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is collaborating with Cisco, CrowdStrike, Google, Microsoft Security, and TrendAI on security integration for the OpenShell runtime, positioning the toolkit as infrastructure beneath enterprise platforms rather than competing with them.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA is positioning NemoClaw as infrastructure that operates beneath, not in competition with, enterprise software platforms such as ServiceNow and Salesforce.

stories.headline: Nvidia debuts Groq 3 LPU at GTC, first chip from $20B Groq acquisition targets agentic inference

key_facts.fact: At GTC 2026 on March 16, Nvidia unveiled the Groq 3 language processing unit (LPU), the first chip resulting from its $20 billion deal with Groq Inc. announced in December 2025, which included hiring founder Jonathan Ross and president Sunny Madra.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia announced it had entered into an agreement to license technology from Groq and hired founder Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra, and other members of the Groq team as part of a $20 billion deal in December.

key_facts.fact: The Groq 3 LPU ships in dedicated Groq 3 LPX server racks holding 256 LPUs with 128 GB of solid-state RAM and 40 petabytes per second of bandwidth, designed for low-latency inference at speeds approaching 1,000 tokens per second per user.
key_facts.excerpt: As generation speeds approach 1,000 tokens per second per user, models move beyond conversation-speed interaction toward speed of thought computing.

key_facts.fact: Unlike Nvidia's general-purpose GPUs, the Groq 3 uses SRAM-packed architecture that moves data directly between on-chip memory modules, eliminating the memory bandwidth bottleneck inherent in GPU designs with separate memory.
key_facts.excerpt: The LPU's architecture functions as a software-defined assembly line for AI workloads, moving data directly between on-chip memory modules without the overhead inherent to Nvidia's general-purpose GPU design.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's Ian Buck said that while GPUs offer greater memory, Groq 3's memory is much faster, designed specifically to support low-latency workloads and large context demands of agentic systems that automate work on behalf of humans.
key_facts.excerpt: Ian Buck, Nvidia's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, said that though the company's GPUs offer greater memory, Groq 3's memory is much faster. It's designed to support low-latency workloads and the large context demands of agentic systems.

key_facts.fact: The Groq 3 LPX is co-designed with Vera Rubin NVL72 to create a heterogeneous inference architecture, pairing large-scale AI factory performance with fast token generation for continuously running multi-agent systems.
key_facts.excerpt: The combination of Vera Rubin NVL72 and LPX enables this heterogeneous architecture, pairing large-scale AI factory performance with the fast token generation needed to power continuously running agentic systems.

stories.headline: Nvidia ships Dynamo 1.0 open-source inference OS, adopted by AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and 20+ partners

key_facts.fact: At GTC 2026, Nvidia announced Dynamo 1.0, a production-grade open-source inference operating system for AI factories, adopted by AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, CoreWeave, Together AI, and Nebius.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA inference platform integrated by cloud service providers, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), along with NVIDIA cloud partners Alibaba Cloud, CoreWeave, Together AI and Nebius.

key_facts.fact: Dynamo 1.0 boosts inference performance of Blackwell GPUs by up to 7x through disaggregated serving and wide expert parallelism, as demonstrated in the SemiAnalysis InferenceX benchmark.
key_facts.excerpt: Dynamo can boost the number of requests served by up to 7x on NVIDIA Blackwell, as demonstrated in the recent SemiAnalysis InferenceX benchmark.

key_facts.fact: AI-native companies including Cursor, Perplexity, ByteDance, Meituan, PayPal, and Pinterest have adopted Dynamo, alongside inference providers Baseten, Deep Infra, and Fireworks.
key_facts.excerpt: adopted by AI-native companies Cursor and Perplexity; inference endpoint providers Baseten, Deep Infra and Fireworks; and global enterprises ByteDance, Meituan, PayPal and Pinterest.

key_facts.fact: Dynamo integrates natively into open-source frameworks including LangChain, llm-d, LMCache, SGLang, and vLLM, and includes features like disaggregated encode/prefill/decode serving, KV cache optimization across memory tiers, and ModelExpress for 7x faster startup.
key_facts.excerpt: Dynamo and NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM optimizations integrate natively into open source frameworks such as LangChain, llm-d, LMCache, SGLang and vLLM to boost inference performance.

stories.headline: Nature Medicine declares 'The AI co-scientist is here' as AI hypotheses reach clinical trials

key_facts.fact: Nature Medicine published a news feature on March 16 titled 'The AI co-scientist is here,' documenting how AI models are evolving from conversational tools to systems that generate scientific hypotheses now being validated in organoids, animal models, and early-stage clinical trials.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence models are evolving from chats to hypotheses. Now their ideas are being validated in organoids and animals — and even in early-stage clinical trials.

key_facts.fact: The article references Google's AI co-scientist system (Gottweis et al., 2025) and documents a trajectory from literature-mining tools like Swanson's 1987 work to modern agentic systems that autonomously generate, test, and validate biomedical hypotheses.
key_facts.excerpt: Gottweis, J. et al. Preprint at https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2502.18864 (2025).

key_facts.fact: The feature highlights that AI drug discovery is producing real results: references include work on antibiotic discovery (Stokes et al., Nature Machine Intelligence 2024) and clinical applications documented in Nature Medicine (Huang et al., 2024), showing the pipeline from AI hypothesis to patient treatment is shortening.
key_facts.excerpt: Stokes, J. M. et al. Nat. Mach. Intell. 6, 845–857 (2024). Huang, K. et al. Nat. Med. 30, 3601–3613 (2024).

key_facts.fact: The editorial arrives amid a wave of AI co-scientist systems: a concurrent paper on arXiv describes CoDHy, an interactive AI system for biomarker-guided drug combination hypothesis generation in cancer research using knowledge graphs and agent-based reasoning.
key_facts.excerpt: We present AI Co-Scientist (CoDHy), an interactive, human-in-the-loop system for biomarker-guided drug combination hypothesis generation in cancer research.

sources.title: From Literature to Hypotheses: An AI Co-Scientist System for Biomarker-Guided Drug Combination Hypothesis Generation

stories.headline: UC Santa Barbara physicists build FERMIACC, an AI agent that generates and tests particle physics theories in minutes

key_facts.fact: Researchers at UC Santa Barbara and the Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics developed FERMIACC, a closed-loop AI agent pipeline that uses OpenAI models alongside established collider physics tools (FeynRules, MadGraph, Pythia) to generate and test hypotheses about unexplained particle physics anomalies.
key_facts.excerpt: The researchers developed a system called FERMIACC, which uses OpenAI models alongside established collider physics tools to generate and test hypotheses about unexplained experimental results.

key_facts.fact: FERMIACC compresses hypothesis generation to seconds and a full simulation-and-analysis cycle to under ten minutes, compared to weeks of work by graduate researchers using traditional methods.
key_facts.excerpt: Hypothesis generation can take seconds and a full simulation and analysis cycle can finish in under ten minutes.

key_facts.fact: The system was built using the OpenAI Agents SDK and operates as a pipeline: generating theoretical hypotheses, running simulations, comparing predicted particle signatures with experimental observations, and evaluating model accuracy against observed results.
key_facts.excerpt: Built with the OpenAI Agents SDK... integrates established physics tools: FeynRules, MadGraph, and Pythia.

key_facts.fact: The team includes KITP postdoc Amalia Madden, UCSB PhD candidate Inigo Valenzuela Lombera, professors Nathaniel Craig and Prateek Agrawal, and postdoc Jessica Howard. The work addresses anomalies in Large Hadron Collider data.
key_facts.excerpt: Working with UCSB PhD candidate Inigo Valenzuela Lombera, Madden began using OpenAI models to help construct and test explanations for unusual results observed in particle collider experiments.

sources.title: UC Santa Barbara physicists test OpenAI models to accelerate particle physics research

stories.headline: Nature Machine Intelligence publishes open-source framework connecting LLMs to robot operating system

key_facts.fact: A paper published in Nature Machine Intelligence on March 16 presents an open-source framework that connects a large language model agent to the robot operating system (ROS), enabling a versatile system for embodied intelligence that translates natural-language instructions into reliable physical robot actions.
key_facts.excerpt: Connecting a large language model agent to the robot operating system enables a versatile framework for embodied intelligence, and we release the complete implementation as freely available open-source code.

key_facts.fact: The framework automatically translates LLM outputs into robot actions with support for interchangeable execution modes (inline code or behaviour trees), learns new atomic skills via imitation, and continually refines them through automated optimization and reflection from human or environmental feedback.
key_facts.excerpt: The agent automatically translates large language model outputs into robot actions, supports interchangeable execution modes (inline code or behaviour trees), learns new atomic skills via imitation, and continually refines them through automated optimization and reflection.

key_facts.fact: Extensive experiments validated the framework, showcasing robustness, scalability, and versatility in diverse scenarios and embodiments, including long-horizon tasks that require the system to chain multiple skills together autonomously.
key_facts.excerpt: Extensive experiments validate the framework, showcasing robustness, scalability and versatility in diverse scenarios and embodiments.

sources.title: A robot operating system framework for using large language models in embodied AI

stories.headline: NC AI demonstrates K-world model for robot intelligence with 80% success rate on advanced tasks

key_facts.fact: On March 16, South Korean company NC AI demonstrated a World Foundation Model (WFM) for robot intelligence, called the K-world model, which achieved an 80% success rate on key advanced robot tasks, confirming the model's potential for practical use.
key_facts.excerpt: NC AI said it carried out training and validation using its own research infrastructure in the world model field... and recorded success rates in key tasks that confirm the model's potential for practical use.

key_facts.fact: Unlike existing World Foundation Models that generate video, reason over it with a vision-language model, and then select actions, NC AI's WFM generates actions directly from latent space information preceding video generation, securing greater efficiency and accuracy.
key_facts.excerpt: Existing WFMs generate video, reason over it with a vision-language model (VLM) and then select actions, while NC AI's WFM uses a model that generates actions directly from latent space information, which precedes video generation, securing efficiency and accuracy.

key_facts.fact: NC AI built the model using its own large-scale computing research infrastructure, challenging global competitors in the physical AI market where world models are considered core technology for the next generation of robot intelligence.
key_facts.excerpt: NC AI said on Monday it demonstrated a World Foundation Model (WFM), a core technology for robot intelligence, and issued a challenge to the global physical AI market.

sources.title: NC AI unveils 'K-world model' research, reaches 80 percent success rate in advanced robot tasks
